48	- **Positive exemplar surfacing (`archy_exemplars`)** ([#138](https://github.com/hslee16/archy/issues/138)). The inverse of `archy_high_risk_modules`: rank the *cleanest* peer module as a copy-me template, because the Constraint Decay HN thread's most-repeated practical finding is that showing an agent a good example beats describing the rule in prose. Design resolved corpus-free and project-relative ([`RESEARCH_METRICS.md` §14c.5](research/RESEARCH_METRICS.md)): archy is the **structural-quality ranker, not the retriever** (similar-code retrieval is the IDE/RAG layer's job and is net-negative when quality is uncontrolled; example *quality* is what dominates ICL outcomes), and "pattern" means a peer group that already exists in the repo, scored by within-group structural health, so it never goes stale. Scoped as an **epic, not a Next item**: gated on the per-module score breakdown (#129), still needs a clean-but-trivial guard and a bench validation that "structurally cleanest peer" tracks "useful exemplar." [Constraint Decay HN; [`FUTURE.md`](FUTURE.md); RESEARCH_METRICS.md §14c.4-5]
49	- **Rule-rot / constraint-staleness detection** ([#139](https://github.com/hslee16/archy/issues/139)). The mirror image of constraint decay: agents obey constraints but cannot tell when a constraint itself is stale, so they satisfy it with inelegant indirection rather than revising it. archy can see the symptom (a `forbid` rule with many `ignore_imports` exceptions; indirection edges that exist only to route around a layer boundary). Scoped as an **epic, not a Next item**: separating "the rule is stale" from "the code is wrong" needs a dead-code-style FP study (the v0.15.0 false-positive lesson is the cautionary precedent) before anything ships. Advisory only if it ever ships. [Constraint Decay HN; [`FUTURE.md`](FUTURE.md); RESEARCH_METRICS.md §14c.4]
50	
51	## Rejected (explicitly will not ship)
52	
53	- **Type-hint coverage in any form (axis or diagnostic).** Empirical study in 2026-05 ([`TYPE_HINT_COVERAGE_EMPIRICS.md`](research/TYPE_HINT_COVERAGE_EMPIRICS.md)) concluded against both axis promotion (independence is the weakest archy has measured, max `|r| = 0.551`; discriminant validity is contested) and diagnostic shipment (mypy / pyright own the typing niche, the signal is not structural, and the "single sensor for everything" framing would dilute archy's graph-shape focus). The bench script and raw numbers stay in `bench/` for future reconsiderations.
54	- **`calls_per_edge` as a 6th score axis.** Empirical study in 2026-05 ([`AXIS_REVIEW.md`](research/AXIS_REVIEW.md)) concluded against axis promotion on directionality / actionability / discriminant-validity grounds even though independence passes. The call data is genuinely useful and shipped as: a diagnostic on `archy score`, the v0.21 call-weighted Newman Q parallel diagnostic, and the LocAgent-style `archy_graph_*` MCP navigation tools.
55	- **HTML output formats for archy commands.** Per the audience principle: agents consume structured JSON and terminal ASCII, not browser-rendered HTML. The original "static HTML trend report" v0.3 stretch goal and the "self-contained HTML for CI artifacts" framing of `archy dsm` are both retired. If a human dashboard is ever needed, third-party tools can consume archy's JSON output.
56	- **Dead-function detection.** Empirical 23-project vulture run in 2026-05 confirmed default-confidence false-positive rates from 10 (msgspec) to 2,017 (django); 15-finding spot-checks on FastAPI / pytest / Django were 15/15 false positives, dominated by Pydantic validators, pytest fixtures, decorator-registered route handlers, and Django's `global_settings.py` string-lookup pattern. Static dead-code detection on real Python is too noisy to fold into a quality signal. Revisit only if archy can ingest a runtime-coverage source.
57	- **Multi-language analysis.** Out of scope; that division of labor with [sentrux](https://github.com/sentrux/sentrux) is settled. archy goes deep on Python instead of broad across languages.
58	- **Code generation or auto-fix.** archy is a sensor, not a fixer. Surfacing the problem is the value.
59	- **DSL or plugin system for layer rules.** YAML stays YAML. If you need more expressive contracts, use `archy contracts` (which wraps import-linter) instead.
60	- **Docstring coverage, test coverage, license scanning, `__all__` consistency, public-API churn, or similar "complete-codebase-health" diagnostics.** Same argument that killed type-hint coverage: better tools own these niches and adding them would dilute archy's graph-shape focus. archy is a graph-shape sensor; it is not the single source of truth for "is this codebase healthy."

34	## Scoring (the headline feature)
35	
36	- ~~**Single quality score**~~ shipped in v0.2.0 as `archy score`. Four sub-metrics (modularity, acyclicity, depth, equality), geometric mean. Side-by-side comparison with sentrux's design in `docs/LEARNINGS.md`.
37	- ~~**Per-commit JSONL history** in `.archy/history.jsonl`~~ shipped in v0.3.0 (`archy score --record`).
38	- ~~**`archy trend`**~~ shipped in v0.3.0 - ASCII sparkline + last-N table.
39	- **Static HTML trend report** - the original stretch goal. Render `.archy/history.jsonl` as a self-contained HTML page with Chart.js so trend can be linked from a CI artifact or dashboard.
40	- **Equality based on per-function CC** - we currently compute Gini over module out-degrees as a proxy. The eventual signal is `gini(per_function_cyclomatic_complexity)`, which requires the cyclomatic-complexity metric above.
41	- **Type-hint coverage as sub-stat or sixth axis** - percentage of public functions with full parameter and return annotations. Differentiated Python signal that no graph-level metric captures. Tree-sitter pass over `FunctionDef` nodes; rides on the same AST scope as cyclomatic complexity. Could ship first as a sub-stat and promote to a score axis if the signal proves load-bearing. 42	- ~~**Hotspots = CC × per-file churn**~~ shipped in v0.18.0 as `archy hotspots` (CLI; module in `src/archy/hotspots.py`). 52	- **Positive exemplar surfacing (`archy_exemplars`)** ([#138](https://github.com/hslee16/archy/issues/138)) - the inverse of `archy_high_risk_modules`: rank the *cleanest* existing module in a structural peer group as a copy-me template, because the Constraint Decay HN thread's most-repeated practical finding is that showing an agent a good example beats describing the rule in prose ("exemplar-based constraints proved phenomenally powerful"; a separate report of ~75-80% style-match when the agent could see how a pattern was already implemented). **Design resolved (corpus-free, project-relative) - see [`RESEARCH_METRICS.md` §14c.5](research/RESEARCH_METRICS.md):** archy must *not* build a corpus of patterns/best-practices (combinatorial and contested per the design-pattern-detection literature; curated catalogs rot like platform-engineering golden paths; semantic similar-code retrieval is already owned by Cursor/Cody/Copilot and net-negative when quality is uncontrolled, "degrading results by up to 15%"). Instead, treat "pattern" as a peer group that *already exists in the repo* (layer / directory / graph community / naming-convention siblings) and "best practice" as best structural health relative to those peers (within-group percentile over `edit_risk`, layer-direction adherence, cycle membership, propagation cost, local Newman Q, `cc_mean`). This makes archy the **structural-quality ranker, not the retriever** (the ICL literature says example *quality* dominates downstream results while *similarity* is the IDE/RAG layer's job), and the exemplar never goes stale because it is recomputed from the live repo every call. Still judge-role (ranks existing code, never generates any) and agent-audience (structured JSON). Honest scope limit: structural health is necessary not sufficient, so the claim is narrow ("structurally cleanest peer," not "best example, period"). **Epic, not a quick win:** gated on the per-module score breakdown ([#129](https://github.com/hslee16/archy/issues/129), ROADMAP "Next"); still needs the clean-but-trivial guard (a one-function module must not win by default) and a 27-project bench validation that "structurally cleanest peer" correlates with "useful exemplar." Diagnostic / MCP tool, never a score axis. [Constraint Decay HN, `arxiv:2605.06445`; RESEARCH_METRICS.md §14c.4-5]
53	- **Rule-rot / constraint-staleness detection** ([#139](https://github.com/hslee16/archy/issues/139)) - the mirror image of constraint decay. The HN thread names a failure the paper does not measure: agents obey constraints but cannot judge when a constraint itself should *change*, so a stale rule gets satisfied by inelegant indirection rather than revised. archy can see the symptom - a `forbid` rule carrying many `ignore_imports` exceptions, or a layer boundary accumulating indirection edges that exist only to route around it (the psycopg-through-db-engine shape from the v0.15.0 lesson). **Treated as an epic, not a quick win:** distinguishing "the rule is stale" from "the code is wrong" is the hard part and needs the same FP-rate discipline as the dead-code study (§12 / the 2026-05 vulture run) before anything ships; without that gate it would manufacture exactly the false-positive noise that demoted the archy.yaml-to-Forbidden translation in v0.15.0. Advisory only if it ever ships. [Constraint Decay, `arxiv:2605.06445`; RESEARCH_METRICS.md §14c.4]
54	- **Type reference edges** - function parameter and return annotations as a third edge type. Useful for catching layer violations that hide behind `if TYPE_CHECKING:` imports. [sentrux: `tags.scm` type-reference query]
55	- **Treemap visualization** - D3 or Observable Plot, wrapped in a static HTML report. Sentrux's signature feature; valuable but not load-bearing for governance use.
56	- **Deterministic contract-check hook for AI sessions.** Empirical finding from the agent-loop test in `governingdocs/backend` (2026-05): a fresh agent caught a forbidden cross-layer import before implementing it, but did so by reading `archy.yaml` + `CLAUDE.md` directly rather than calling `archy_check` / `archy_contracts`. The MCP-tool angle's marginal value over "agent reads docs" is narrower than the hypothesis assumed - it shows up mainly when rules live only in `.importlinter` (no archy.yaml) or when violations are transitive multi-hop. To make contract-check feedback deterministic regardless of agent disposition, ship a Claude Code Stop hook that runs `archy contracts` once per task and surfaces violations into the agent's context. Per-task cost: ~3-5s wall, ~150-600 tokens. PostToolUse-on-Edit fires too often (5-15x per task, edit-thrashing noise). Project-side configuration only; archy doesn't need new code. Worth shipping as a documented snippet in `docs/AGENT_LOOP.md`, not a feature.
57	- ~~**Pre-commit hook + GitHub Action**~~ shipped in v0.4.1/v0.4.2 - see `README.md` for usage.

git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat(render): archy render -> self-contained HTML (dsm + trend views)

Branch A of the visualization surface (#283), scoped to the two views that
need no layout engine. `archy render --view dsm|trend` writes one
self-contained HTML file: inline SVG, inline CSS, no JavaScript, no vendored
bundle, no external request, no embedded wall-clock time. Byte-stable for a
fixed input, so it snapshot-tests and two exports diff cleanly.

The `graph` view is deferred, not dropped. It is the only view that forces a
vendored force-layout engine into the wheel, and it is the weakest of the
three against the anti-theater gate. Deferring it holds Branch A to the same
usage-signal bar the spec already applies to the `archy_render` MCP tool, and
that the research docs apply to their own candidates. Exit condition recorded
in SPEC_VISUALIZATION.md 3a so the deferral cannot silently become a wontfix.

Red means what the ordering actually encodes. `row > col` is a back-edge only
under a topological ordering; under community or layer grouping the block
order is not a dependency order, so flagging it there is noise (on archy
itself it painted 168 of 243 cells red). The renderer flags back-edges under
--group=topological and block-crossing edges otherwise, and says which in the
legend.

Also reconciles the docs: ROADMAP listed HTML output as an explicit non-goal.
That rejection is narrowed rather than quietly ignored, to HTML as a mode of
the agent-facing surface, with the human-governor export called out as the
one deliberate exception to the audience principle.

Closes #284

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

Base directory for this skill: /Users/hosanglee/.claude/plugins/cache/deepwork-plugins/deepwork/0.14.0/skills/review

# DeepWork Review

Run automated code reviews on the current branch based on `.deepreview` config files.

## Routing — Check Before Proceeding

**STOP and redirect** if either of these applies:

- User wants to **configure, create, or modify** review rules (e.g., "add a security review", "set up reviews for our API layer") → use the `configure_reviews` skill instead
- User wants to **add a doc-sync rule** (keep a documentation file in sync with source files) → call `start_workflow` with `job_name="deepwork_reviews"` and `workflow_name="add_document_update_rule"`

Only proceed past this section if the user wants to **run** reviews.

## Pre-flight — Verify Agent Availability

Before running reviews, check that the `deepwork:reviewer` agent is available. If it does not appear in the agents list (i.e., the Agent tool does not list `deepwork:reviewer` as a valid `subagent_type`), **STOP** and tell the user:

> The `deepwork:reviewer` agent is not available. Please run `/reload-plugins` to pick up the latest plugin updates, then try again.

Do not proceed with reviews until the agent is available.

## How to Run

1. Call the `mcp__deepwork__get_review_instructions` tool directly:
   - **No arguments** to review the current branch's changes (auto-detects via git diff against the main branch).
   - **With `files`** to review only specific files: `mcp__deepwork__get_review_instructions(files=["src/app.py", "src/lib.py"])`. When provided, only reviews whose include/exclude patterns match the given files will be returned. Use this when the user asks to review a particular file or set of files rather than the whole branch.
   - **If the result says no rules are configured**: Ask the user if they'd like to auto-discover and set up rules. If yes, invoke the `/deepwork` skill with the `deepwork_reviews` job's `discover_rules` workflow. Stop here — do not proceed with running reviews if there are no rules.
2. The output will list review tasks to invoke in parallel. Each task has `description`, `subagent_type`, and `prompt` fields — these map directly to the Agent tool parameters. Launch all of them as parallel agents.
3. **While review agents run**, check for a changelog and open PR (see below).
4. Collect the results from all review agents.

## Changelog & PR Description Check

Run this concurrently with the review agents (step 2 above) — don't wait for reviews to finish first.

1. Check if the project has a changelog file (e.g., `CHANGELOG.md`, `CHANGELOG`, `CHANGES.md`).
2. If a changelog exists and there are commits on the current branch beyond the main branch:
   - Read the changelog and the branch's commit log (`git log main..HEAD --oneline`).
   - Verify the changelog's unreleased/current section accurately reflects what the branch does. If entries are missing, outdated, or inaccurate, update the changelog.
3. If a PR is open for the current branch (check with `gh pr view`):
   - If you updated the changelog, also verify the PR description matches. Update it with `gh pr edit` if needed.
   - If the changelog was already accurate, skip the PR description check.

## Acting on Results

For each finding from the review agents:

- **Obviously good changes with no downsides** (e.g., fixing a typo, removing an unused import, adding a missing null check): make the change immediately without asking. When in doubt, ask.
- **Everything else** (refactors, style changes, architectural suggestions, anything with trade-offs):
  1. Use AskUserQuestion to ask the user about each finding **individually**. Do not group issues together unless they are the same issue occurring in multiple files; otherwise, use AskUserQuestion to ask about each issue separately. This lets the user make separate decisions on each item.
  2. For each question, provide several concrete fix approaches as options when there are reasonable alternatives (e.g., "Update the spec to match the code" vs "Update the code to match the spec" vs "Skip").
  3. If a finding seems minor or debatable, include an option to suppress that error in the future — such as a clarification to the rule if it is too narrow, or a comment on the offending content if comments work in that context.
  4. Be concise — quote the key finding, don't dump the full review.

When a finding is dismissed (user chooses "Skip" or you determine it's not actionable for this PR), call `mcp__deepwork__mark_review_as_passed` with the review's ID so it won't re-run on subsequent iterations.

## Iterate

After making any changes:

1. Call `mcp__deepwork__get_review_instructions` with `files` set to **only the files you edited** during this iteration. This scopes the re-review to your changes rather than re-reviewing the entire branch.
2. Repeat the cycle (run → act on results → run again) until a clean run — one where all review agents return no findings, or all remaining findings have been explicitly skipped by the user.
3. On subsequent runs, you only need to re-run tasks that had findings last time — skip tasks that were clean.
4. Reviews that already passed are automatically skipped as long as reviewed files remain unchanged.

497:Empirically rejected (kept here so they don't get re-proposed): type-hint coverage in any form, `calls_per_edge` as a 6th axis, HTML output formats, dead-function detection, multi-language analysis. See [`docs/ROADMAP.md`](docs/ROADMAP.md#rejected-explicitly-will-not-ship) for the evidence behind each.
- **v0.16, call-graph edges** as a second edge type: `kinds`, `call_lines`, `call_count` on every edge; `total_calls` / `calls_per_edge` on `archy score`; static import-alias resolution per LocAgent's invoke-edge framing.
- **v0.17, per-function cyclomatic complexity**: per-module `function_count` / `cc_sum` / `cc_max` / `cc_mean` on every internal node; project-wide aggregates on `archy score`; tree-sitter McCabe walker in `src/archy/complexity.py`. Promoted to the `complexity` score axis in v0.20 (recalibrated `/8` in v0.23).
- **v0.18, `archy hotspots`**: per-file refactor-priority ranking from `cc_sum x git-commit-count`; single rename-aware `git log --name-status -M` pass (folds pre-rename history onto the current path); Tornhill/CodeScene's "Code Red" formulation; filters zero-CC and zero-churn rows. MCP surface (`archy_hotspots`) followed in v0.19.
- **v0.21, call-weighted Newman Q** as a *parallel diagnostic* on `archy score` (not an axis replacement): the gap between unweighted and weighted Q flags mismatch between import-graph and call-graph community structure ([`docs/research/CALL_WEIGHTED_Q_EMPIRICS.md`](docs/research/CALL_WEIGHTED_Q_EMPIRICS.md)).
- **v0.22, `archy dsm`** (Design Structure Matrix): CLI + `archy_dsm` MCP tool with `--group=community|layer|topological`, `--weight=imports|calls`, `--focus`/`--package`, and `--diff` for back-edge regression detection. Visualization-only per [`docs/research/DSM_EMPIRICS.md`](docs/research/DSM_EMPIRICS.md): no DSM-derived score axis or diagnostic scalar.

**Install / distribution**

- **v0.25, Claude Code plugin** (`plugins/claude/`): bundles the MCP server registration and the canonical `archy` skill into an installable unit.
- **v0.26, agent-detecting installer** (`archy install` / `archy uninstall`): auto-detects which clients (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, opencode, Continue) are present, writes each one's MCP stanza and rules file, and seeds Claude's `permissions.allow`. Adapter registry in `src/archy/install/`; user docs in [`docs/INSTALL.md`](docs/INSTALL.md).

Empirically rejected (kept here so they don't get re-proposed): type-hint coverage in any form, `calls_per_edge` as a 6th axis, HTML output formats, dead-function detection, multi-language analysis. See [`docs/ROADMAP.md`](docs/ROADMAP.md#rejected-explicitly-will-not-ship) for the evidence behind each.

See [`docs/FUTURE.md`](docs/FUTURE.md) for the longer list and [`docs/LEARNINGS.md`](docs/LEARNINGS.md) for design notes.

**Lines:** 152, 345, 503, 567, 652, 654, 656, 751, 753, 755, 831, 833, 1115, 1117, 1248, 1253, 1255 (18 occurrences total)

**Rule violated:** "DRY: no copy-pasted blocks that should be a shared helper" (from the review's concrete criteria list).

**Quote of the offending construct** — the same two-line shape is copy-pasted 18 times with only the variable name, comparison, and message text changed. Representative examples:

```python

if min_size < 1:
    raise click.ClickException(f"--min-size must be >= 1; got {min_size}")
```

```python

```

```python

if top_n < 1:

```

```python
# lines 654, 656 (coupling command)
if min_support < 1:
    raise click.ClickException(f"--min-support must be >= 1; got {min_support}")
if not 0.0 < min_confidence <= 1.0:
    raise click.ClickException(f"--min-confidence must be in (0, 1]; got {min_confidence}")
```

```python
# lines 1115, 1117 (dsm command)
if focus_depth < 0:
    raise click.ClickException(f"--focus-depth must be >= 0; got {focus_depth}")
if max_nodes < 1:
    raise click.ClickException(f"--max-nodes must be >= 1; got {max_nodes}")
```

The identical pattern (`if <condition on value>: raise click.ClickException(f"--<flag> must be <constraint>; got {<value>}")`) also recurs at lines 291, 503, 652, 751, 753, 755, 831, 833, 1248, 1253.

**Why this violates the rule:** Every one of these blocks is structurally identical boilerplate — a bound check on a CLI option followed by a `click.ClickException` raised with an f-string that names the flag, states the constraint, and echoes the bad value. Only the flag name, the numeric/relational constraint, and the local variable differ. This is exactly the kind of copy-pasted block the criterion calls out as something that "should be a shared helper" rather than being hand-duplicated at each of the 15 command functions. It also lets duplication drift into inconsistency: `what_to_refactor_next` (not in the line list above, checked separately) uses `top_n <= 0` while every other command uses `top_n < 1` for the same semantic "must be positive" check — a symptom of the logic not being centralized.

**Suggested fix:** Extract a small shared validator, e.g.:

```python
def _require(ok: bool, flag: str, constraint: str, value: object) -> None:
    """Raise a uniform ClickException for a failed CLI option bound-check."""
    if not ok:
        raise click.ClickException(f"--{flag} must be {constraint}; got {value}")
```

and replace each call site with a one-liner, e.g.:

```python
_require(min_size >= 1, "min-size", ">= 1", min_size)
_require(top_n >= 1, "top", ">= 1", top_n)
_require(focus_depth >= 0, "focus-depth", ">= 0", focus_depth)
_require(0.0 < min_confidence <= 1.0, "min-confidence", "in (0, 1]", min_confidence)
```

This collapses the 18 near-identical blocks into a single reusable helper and, as a side effect, fixes the `top_n <= 0` vs. `top_n < 1` inconsistency by centralizing the constraint expression per call site.

This was the only violation found across all the criteria checked (import ordering, PEP 604 typing, naming, pydantic value objects, `pathlib.Path` usage, line length, comment WHY-vs-WHAT accuracy — all passed). Because this DRY violation exists, the review result remains FAIL, and I have not called `mark_review_as_passed`.</result>

input.command:
gh issue create --label "good first issue" --label "help wanted" --title "refactor(cli): extract a shared bound-check helper for the 18 duplicated ClickException validations" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
`src/archy/cli.py` repeats the same option bound-check in 18 places across 15 commands:

```python
if min_size < 1:
    raise click.ClickException(f"--min-size must be >= 1; got {min_size}")
```

Only the flag name, the constraint, and the variable change. Occurrences: lines 152, 291, 345, 503, 567, 652, 654, 656, 751, 753, 755, 831, 833, 1115, 1117, 1248, 1253, 1255 (approximate; they move as the file changes).

## Why it is worth doing

Not just line count. The duplication has already drifted: `what-to-refactor-next` uses `top_n <= 0` where every other command uses `top_n < 1` for the same "must be positive" check. Centralizing the expression is what stops that.

## Suggested shape

```python
def _require(ok: bool, flag: str, constraint: str, value: object) -> None:
    """Raise a uniform ClickException for a failed CLI option bound-check."""
    if not ok:
        raise click.ClickException(f"--{flag} must be {constraint}; got {value}")
```

Call sites become:

```python
_require(min_size >= 1, "min-size", ">= 1", min_size)
_require(0.0 < min_confidence <= 1.0, "min-confidence", "in (0, 1]", min_confidence)
```

## Constraints

- **Error messages must not change.** Existing tests assert on them (`assert "--last" in result.output` and similar), and the message text is user-facing. Keep the `--{flag} must be {constraint}; got {value}` output byte-identical.
- Normalize the `top_n <= 0` outlier to match the rest while you are there.
- No behavior change otherwise; `uv run pytest` should stay green.

Found by the local review tooling while reviewing #284; left out of that PR because 15 of the touched commands have nothing to do with it.
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -2

gh pr create --title "feat(render): archy render -> self-contained HTML (dsm + trend views)" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Closes #284. Branch A of the visualization surface (#283), **scoped to two of the three proposed views**.

## What ships

`archy render PATH --view dsm|trend [--out FILE]` writes one self-contained HTML file: inline SVG, inline CSS, **no JavaScript, no vendored bundle, no external request, no embedded wall-clock time**. Byte-stable for a fixed input, so it snapshot-tests and two exports diff cleanly.

- **`--view dsm`**: the matrix as SVG, row labels, column index ruler, block boundaries, per-cell tooltips, plus a counts strip (modules / edges / flagged / blocks) and an index table. Honors `--group`, `--weight`, `--focus`, `--focus-depth`, `--package`.
- **`--view trend`**: one sparkline per axis over `.archy/history.jsonl`, each with its numeric range and window delta, plus the last-N table. Honors `--last`.

Light and dark themes via `prefers-color-scheme`. Output goes to stdout unless `--out` is given.

## The `graph` view is deferred, not dropped

It is the only view that forces a vendored force-layout engine into the wheel, and it is the weakest of the three against the spec's anti-theater gate: a node-link diagram is present in every tool, whereas DSM cell positions and a score trajectory are things text conveys poorly.

Deferring it holds Branch A to the same **usage-signal** bar `SPEC_VISUALIZATION.md` §6.3 already applies to the `archy_render` MCP tool, and that `PATTERN_DETECTION_EMPIRICS.md` / `CONSTRAINT_AWARE_ORCHESTRATION_SYNTHESIS.md` / `INLOOP_PREVALENCE_EMPIRICS.md` apply to their own candidates. An exit condition is recorded in §3a so the deferral cannot silently become a wontfix.

Dropping it also meant the vendoring constraint disappeared entirely: both shipped views are static, so the original "vendor the JS in-repo" requirement became "no JS at all", which is strictly stronger and cost nothing.

## Red means what the ordering actually encodes

The first working build exposed a signal-honesty bug worth calling out. `row > col` is a **back-edge** only under a topological ordering. Under community or layer grouping the block order is not a dependency order, so flagging `row > col` there is noise: on archy itself it painted **168 of 243 cells red**.

The renderer now flags back-edges under `--group=topological` and block-crossing edges under `--group=community|layer`, states which in the legend, and suppresses the back-edge count where it would be meaningless. On archy under community grouping that is 49 flagged cells, and the block structure is readable. A view that colors cells by a property its ordering does not encode is theater even when the underlying number is real.

## Docs reconciled, not quietly contradicted

`ROADMAP.md` listed HTML output as an explicit non-goal. Rather than ignore it, the rejection is **narrowed** to HTML as a mode of the agent-facing surface, with `archy render` recorded as the one deliberate exception to the audience principle: it serves the human governor, exports only signals archy already computes, and does not sit in the agent loop. `FUTURE.md`'s "static HTML trend report" stretch goal is marked shipped; the treemap entry now records why it was *not* picked up.

## Verification

- 27 new tests (21 unit + 6 CLI). Full suite **916 passed**, 2 skipped.
- `ruff check` clean, `ruff format` clean, `mypy` clean on the new module.
- Rendered both views against archy itself and inspected them in a browser.
- Dogfood: score 0.6705 (from 0.6695), 0 cycles, `archy check` clean. `archy impact` confirms the blast radius is `archy.cli` plus tests.

## Out of scope, ticketed instead

Local review surfaced two pre-existing DRY issues in code this PR does not touch. Filed rather than folded in: #317 (duplicated package setup in `test_cli.py`) and #318 (18 duplicated CLI bound-checks, which hide a real `<= 0` vs `< 1` inconsistency). Both are good-first-issue shaped.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

50	- **PROCESS (3 review rounds, verdict never moved, supporting detail kept breaking):** 16 adversarial findings, then **7 MORE found in my own corrections**, including **a fabricated figure introduced while fixing a fabrication** ($15.4/$13.8 for codegraph; real = OkHttp $0.23 vs $0.20) and **twice applying a standard to others I broke myself** (quoting only the worst point of my key source while indicting CodeScene for "up to" framing). §10 of the note logs all of them. **Lesson: after a correction pass, always re-verify the corrections themselves.**
51	- **Git lesson:** merging a stacked PR with `--delete-branch` **auto-closes the child PR and a closed PR's base CANNOT be retargeted** (#314 died this way, replaced by #315). Merge the parent WITHOUT --delete-branch, or retarget the child to main first.

53	**Pre-existing non-duplicate backlog:**
54	- **#129** per-module score (unblocks #138 exemplars).
55	- **#145** archy review brief (strongest standalone feature - per-PR structural review brief for human judgment).

60	
61	- **Release rule:** cut a release only on a user-visible `src/archy/` change. bench/tests/docs/plugin-only changes do NOT trigger a release.

86	
87	**Question (#289):** can an archy structural pre-edit brief reduce the exploratory reads a coding agent does before its first edit? 88	
89	**Built + ran it.** Added **arm C (context-injection)** to the #259 harness (PR **#294**, branch `alee/armc-read-reduction-289`): inject a 581-tok archy brief into the prompt, measure reads-before-first-edit. New harness code = `pre_edit_reads`/`pre_edit_distinct_files`/`pre_edit_input_tokens`/`made_edit` on the parser, `run_variant(prompt_prefix=)`, `run_arm_c`, A-vs-C `summarize`, `--mode ac`. - **Git lesson:** merging a stacked PR with `--delete-branch` **auto-closes the child PR and a closed PR's base CANNOT be retargeted** (#314 died this way, replaced by #315). Merge the parent WITHOUT --delete-branch, or retarget the child to main first.

**Pre-existing non-duplicate backlog:**
- **#129** per-module score (unblocks #138 exemplars).
- **#145** archy review brief (strongest standalone feature - per-PR structural review brief for human judgment).
- Also open: #139 rule-rot/constraint-staleness, #135 layer-presence check, #134 static-fragility (good-first), #132 opt-in hooks.
- **Leave good-first #199/#238/#239 for outside contributors** ([[feedback_leave_good_first_issues]]).

## Durable conventions

- **Release rule:** cut a release only on a user-visible `src/archy/` change. bench/tests/docs/plugin-only changes do NOT trigger a release.
- **Plugin pin bump** only on a BC MCP change or a new tool; additive params/fields don't bump it.
- **PyPI publish** has an env gate; I approve it via API when a release was actually requested ([[feedback_pypi_gate_approval]]).
- **Always review via DeepWork** (incl. adversarial), never the code-review skill ([[feedback_use_deepwork_review]]). `.deepreview` is local-only/gitignored ([[feedback_deepreview_local_only]]).
- **Value objects = frozen pydantic** (`class X(BaseModel): model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True)`), NOT `NamedTuple`/`@dataclass` (22 BaseModel value objects in src/archy). **ONE documented exception: `coupling.CoChangeData` stays a NamedTuple** - hot path, `pair_support` holds millions of dict entries on large repos, never serialized, so pydantic per-item validation is pure cost. Do NOT let a review re-flag it. The DeepWork `python_code_review` rule enforces this; when it flags a NamedTuple, convert unless it's the CoChangeData-shaped case (huge + hot + never-serialized). Migrating: swap `_asdict()`->`model_dump()`, keep computed values as plain `@property` (so `model_dump()` excludes them, matching `_asdict()`).
- **Dogfood archy on itself** as the dev loop ([[feedback_dogfood_archy]]); overall score baseline ~0.67.

## Durable research findings (duplicate detection)

- **~50% precision is the syntactic CEILING**, not a bug: up to ~71% of real clones are benign (Kapser & Godfrey); no production tool solves benign-vs-refactorable syntactically (the boundary is semantic).
- **Co-change is the precision lever** (>94% in the literature): a cluster whose members co-change is refactorable; one that never co-changes is benign. Shipped as `demote_independent` (#242).
- **Exact AST-shape hashing is Type-1/2 only** and misses Type-3 (gapped) clones, the plurality of real clones. Fixed by the token-multiset overlap primitive (#246, opt-in).
- Precision varies by domain: ORM/SDK ~80%, scientific/ML ~33% (mostly test-code + vendored dup) -> path-scoping demotes test/vendored (#247).

## 2026-07-06: cleanliness-paper research -> tickets #259-#262 (all claims adversarially fact-checked first)

**User asked to research arXiv 2605.20049v1 "Does Code Cleanliness Affect Coding Agents? A Controlled Minimal-Pair Study" (SonarSource; HN 48798815), apply to archy, validate every point before filing tickets.** Ran 5 parallel adversarial validation agents against the primary source + web.

**Paper's verified findings:** pass rate FLAT (0.913 clean vs 0.921 messy, -0.9pp) - cleanliness does NOT change task success; footprint shrinks on clean side: input tokens -7.1%, output -8.5%, reasoning chars -11.1%, messages -7.0%; **file revisitation -34% aggregate** (largest effect; "~a third", NOT "halved" - halved is multi-module-track-only). Effect concentrates on MULTI-MODULE tasks. Mechanism = grep-targetability. Config: Sonnet 4.6 / Claude Code, Python+Java only.

**Corrections baked into the tickets (guard against overclaiming):** (1) "module-dependency tooling targets the effect layer" is MY INFERENCE, not a paper finding (paper's lever was SonarQube LINE-level rules; only the TASKS are cross-module). (2) god-object-split "worse" is PER-TASK (Case 2 +8% input tokens), NEUTRAL at track level (+0.1%). (3) TOKENS not dollars (§6: nonlinear). (4) "Opus 4.6 built the variants" is an HN comment (id 48800911), NOT the paper - paper never names the construction model. (5) "duplication misleads agent grep" is practitioner anecdote (HN 48800345/48800118) + indirect academic (arXiv 2510.13859); NO controlled study isolates duplication; do NOT cite 2605.20049 for it. Agent-cost-as-eval-axis prior art = SWE-Effi arXiv 2509.09853.

**#259 is the recommended flagship:** produces archy's own controlled number (apply top recommendation, measure agent token footprint + revisitation before/after, with the unrelated-test-regression gate the paper lacks). New bench category - current bench/ measures architecture metrics, not agent tokens.

## 2026-07-21: #289 stencil 'prewalk' read-reduction -> arm-C bench -> documented NON-RESULT

**Question (#289):** can an archy structural pre-edit brief reduce the exploratory reads a coding agent does before its first edit? (stencil.so/blog/prewalk: the agent bill is O(reads), not O(edits); prewalk's actual win is a warm-*trajectory* handoff, which a tool artifact CANNOT replicate - archy is weak for that; its only shot is (A) substitution, which it already half-ships via `invariant_brief`/`impact`/`graph(focus)` but never measured.)

**Built + ran it.** Added **arm C (context-injection)** to the #259 harness (PR **#294**, branch `alee/armc-read-reduction-289`): inject a 581-tok archy brief into the prompt, measure reads-before-first-edit. New harness code = `pre_edit_reads`/`pre_edit_distinct_files`/`pre_edit_input_tokens`/`made_edit` on the parser, `run_variant(prompt_prefix=)`, `run_arm_c`, A-vs-C `summarize`, `--mode ac`. Config: flask @ 36e4a82, `claude-sonnet-5`, teardown-ordering task (true surface 3 files: sansio/app.py + app.py + ctx.py), brief precision 0.33 (named 9 files, 3 on-surface).

**Result = NON-RESULT.** Pooled **N=22** (a stalled headless claude at run 22 killed, unpaired arm dropped): `pre_edit_reads` median delta **-2.0, 14/8 pairs, sign p=0.286**. An N=10 hint (median -3.5, p=0.109) **did NOT survive doubling N**. `pre_edit_distinct_files` UNCHANGED (delta=0) - the agent found the ~3-file spine unaided, so **no headroom for any brief on an easy/grep-able task**. `num_turns` nominally -5 (p=0.041) but FAILS multiple-comparison correction and is not a read count (do NOT relabel as read reduction). 0 regressions throughout. **NO-GO on an `archy brief` feature, on EVIDENCE** (effect regressed to null on more data) - the anti-theater gate working: the N=10 hint would've shipped theater.

**Durable lesson:** briefs help where an agent WOULD flounder (large/unfamiliar repo, non-grep-discoverable surface, weak/cheap executor a-la prewalk's frontier->cheap), NOT on easy tasks where it finds the spine itself. The path to a significant brief effect is a harder *setting*, not a better *brief* (breadth was flat even with the noisy brief, so lifting brief precision has a weak prior). A small true effect won't clear significance at N~22 anyway (needs N~50-100 or a bigger effect). Findings note `docs/research/PREWALK_READ_REDUCTION_SYNTHESIS.md` (§6 result, §7 headroom-scoping); result table in `bench/agent_footprint_results.md`.

**Tickets (all CLOSED 2026-07-21):** #289 research (findings note merged PR #294); #290 brief precision metric, #291 task-conditioned focus, #293 metric split - all CLOSED as mooted by the non-result (contingent on the brief helping, which it did not; reopen only for a harder-setting rerun per §7); #292 power-to-N30 CLOSED (answered by the N=22 null); #295 pydantic migration DONE (PR #296). **Net: the whole #289 arc is closed - a documented non-result, no feature, nothing left open.** Reopen path if ever revisited: a HARDER setting (unfamiliar/large repo, non-grep surface, weak/cheap executor), NOT a better brief.

content.text:
**PR #319 is open** and all reviews passed: https://github.com/hslee16/Archy/pull/319

**What shipped** (scoped exactly as we discussed):
- `archy render --view dsm|trend --out FILE` writes one self-contained HTML file. No JavaScript at all, not just no CDN, since both views are static and need no layout engine. Byte-stable, light/dark aware, stdout by default.
- `--view graph` deferred behind a usage signal, with an exit condition written into `SPEC_VISUALIZATION.md` §3a so it can't quietly become a wontfix.

**Two things worth flagging that came out of actually building it:**

1. **A real signal-honesty bug the design would not have caught.** `row > col` is a back-edge only under topological ordering. Under the default `--group=community`, block order isn't a dependency order, so the first build painted 168 of 243 cells red on archy itself. The renderer now flags back-edges under topological and block-crossing edges otherwise, and says which in the legend. Worth knowing: `summarize_dsm` still reports `back_edge_count` under every grouping. That's fine in agent JSON, but anything that *renders* it needs the same distinction.

2. **ROADMAP listed HTML output as an explicit non-goal.** Rather than ignore it, I narrowed the rejection to "HTML on agent-facing commands" and recorded `archy render` as one deliberate exception to the audience principle. The repo would otherwise have contradicted itself in two places.

**Verification:** 27 new tests, full suite 916 passed, ruff/mypy clean, both views rendered and visually inspected. Dogfood: 0.6705 (from 0.6695), 0 cycles, `archy check` clean.

**Also filed:**
- **#316** codegraph research, scoped to capability and positioning. The benchmark forensics are already closed in `TOKEN_REDUCTION_CLAIMS.md` §8, so the ticket points there and forbids redoing it. The questions it actually forces are the uncomfortable ones: is Python-only defensible or just rationalized resourcing, does symbol-level granularity expose something module-level can't, and what is archy's remaining honest claim in one falsifiable sentence.
- **#317** and **#318**, both pre-existing DRY findings from review in code this PR never touched. #318 is the more interesting one: 18 duplicated CLI bound-checks that hide a real `top_n <= 0` vs `< 1` inconsistency.

Release is queued for after you merge. Say the word and I'll bump to 0.42.0, tag, and approve the PyPI gate.
